desc: Derive core model: each ball must travel its color's permutation cycle to X; box X is never operated; per-color requirement is the chain of boxes from farthest ball down to distance 1, fired in decreasing-distance order; one fire per box suffices unless the two chains conflict.
Establish impossibility condition: any red ball off X's P-cycle or blue ball off X's Q-cycle → -1; otherwise always feasible.

Establish min operations = length of shortest common supersequence of R (P-cycle boxes, decreasing dist, up to max red distance) and B (same for Q); with distinct elements, SCS = |R| + |B| − LCS, and LCS = LIS of R-positions in B-order (O(N log N)).
Hand-verify model on all four samples (4, 0, -1, 8) plus a custom conflicting-chains case (answer 3 = SCS of [1,2] and [2,1]).
Implement the solution: cycle walk from X for P and Q (dist(cyc[k]) = (L−k) mod L), feasibility check, build R and B sequences, LIS via bisect, print answer or -1, with fast stdin reading.
Review implementation for edge cases: balls only at X (M=0, empty chain), no balls (0), self-loop at X, 1-indexing, N=2e5 performance; remove dead code.
